subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Solar Panels in Space: Powering the Void
description: A fast breakdown of Solar Panels in Space: Powering the Void for builders.

hook.text: The ISS has solar panels the size of a football field. They generate just enough power to run about 40 average homes.

buildup.text: Space solar panels use triple-junction gallium arsenide cells — far more efficient than rooftop silicon but extremely expensive.

discovery.text: Panels rotate to track the sun as the station orbits. Sun-tracking gimbals adjust every few seconds during the 90-minute orbit.

twist.text: Every 90 minutes, the ISS enters Earth's shadow for 36 minutes. Batteries must store enough energy to power it through darkness.

climax.text: NASA recently upgraded the ISS batteries from nickel-hydrogen to lithium-ion. The new ones are half the size and last longer.

punchline.text: Sun for 54 minutes. Dark for 36. Every orbit. Every day.

quiz.question: How often does the ISS enter Earth's shadow during its orbit?
options: Once per day, during a 6-hour nighttime period on one side of Earth
Every 90 minutes, spending about 36 minutes in shadow each orbit
Twice per orbit, for about 10 minutes each time it passes the poles
